classifier: scripts/problem_types.py (same file used on every dataset)
metric: ABSOLUTE rate per 1000 sampled rows. Share-of-classified was rejected: its denominator is whatever the classifier could label on that dataset (55%..100%), so a type's share partly measures the classifier's coverage drift.
sampling: fixed stride, deterministic, reproducible from the file length; n=2000 per dataset except HumanEval (all 164) and the RL pool (all survivors)
boundary: ROW != PROBLEM. HumanEval rows are distinct problems; sftA/RL rows are extracted pairs and one repository contributes many; pretrain rows are whole FILES. This table supports order-of-magnitude supply differences (5-8x), not fine ranking. pretrain is FILES mode: no problem/solution boundary exists, so those numbers are topic rates over files and are not directly comparable to the pairs-mode columns.
access: read-only throughout. sc2/apps rebuilt into /tmp by importing the production renderer with OUT_DIR rebound; the RL pool filtered in memory by the builder's own dedup rule; nothing written under the pod repo.
mix_weights_source: data/mix_v41_gate.json (the authoritative gate-mix domain list and weights; 1e 2026-09-25: scan exactly this list, nothing else)
weighted_exposure: sum over mix domains of (weight x rate/1000). An INDICATOR of topical exposure, NOT a measurement that the model saw tasks of that type: every mix domain is FILES mode, so a rate is topics-per-document, and a document mentioning a count is not a problem requiring counting. en_c4 is excluded from the code-only column.

sampled_of: 10,776 rendered pairs (stride 5); measured on the ORIGINAL question text
note: the renderer keeps only the starter signature, so measuring the rendered prompt reads 990/2000 unclassified (a signature-only string vs HumanEval's docstring); on the question text it is 141.

reproduced read-only with the builder's own rule (sha1(norm_text(prompt)), survivor=max test count); survivor count and per-file counts match rl_code_global_dedup_stats.json exactly. Supersedes the earlier partial scan of 27+539 rows.

sampled_of: 1 shard of 283 (stride 10); FILES mode, no problem boundary

note: content is SYNTHETIC task-shaped text ('Write a Python function `draw_star_square(n)` ...'), unlike starcoder's whole repository files; it is why unclassified collapses to 0.2%.
